reasons.lme: Paid for its generators.
reasons.hac: Market keeps the plants running.
reasons.riw: Paying the Exchange for its own air.
reasons.fam: Merchants profit from the dark.

history.history: In history: Reactor Two scrammed, and a 22-sol brownout fell across Domes 2 to 5.

history.title: Bill at First Reading
history.question: The Self-Government Bill passed 31 to 19. Will you let it stand?
history.body: Colonial Assembly, first reading: 31 for, 19 against. 26 needed. The Charter bench walked out. Duct-drums in the gallery.

answers.text: Let it stand; recognise the vote
answers.sub: No Charter veto at first reading.

reasons.cas: Its bill stands untouched.
reasons.fam: Self-government one reading closer.
reasons.mca: Secession advancing unvetoed.
reasons.aco: Its chain to Geneva fraying.

answers.gripWhy: An elected vote respected.

answers.text: Demand a union allocation clause in it
answers.sub: Self-government only with RIWU board seats.

reasons.riw: Its seat written into the new order.
reasons.fam: Workers and Mars-born together.
reasons.lme: Union seats over its trade.
reasons.hac: Councils over its ice plant.
reasons.cas: Its bill rewritten from Dome 1.

history.history: In history: The Colonial Assembly passed the Self-Government Bill's first reading 31 to 19.

situations.title: Six Days of Slack

carrier.name: Noor Haddad-Lindqvist
carrier.role: Chief Systems Engineer, Habitat Systems Directorate

situations.question: Governor, will you ration every dome or cut Ice Field shifts?
situations.body: Quarterly margin report: oxygen at 186 days. The Charter floor is 180. That leaves six days of slack. The reserve slips five to six days a month. The board offers two cuts: 8 percent air and power in every dome, or fewer RIWU shifts at Ice Field 7.

answers.text: Impose the 8 percent ration colony-wide.
answers.sub: Every dome breathes less; the margin line holds longer.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, and the margin board is obeyed.
reasons.riw: The cut falls on everyone, not only the crews.
reasons.lme: Rationed power dims the arcade and kills trade hours.
reasons.cas: A ration imposed without one vote in the chamber.
reasons.mca: A governor who guards the floor keeps Geneva calm.

answers.gripWhy: Rationing by order, enforced at every meter.

answers.text: Cut Ice Field 7 shifts; keep the arcade lit.
answers.sub: Fewer union shifts; commerce keeps full power.

reasons.lme: Shops stay open while the cut lands elsewhere.
reasons.riw: Our crews lose pay so the arcade keeps its lights.
reasons.hsd: Fewer shifts mean less load on the electrolysis halls.
reasons.fam: Tube families pay for the merchants' comfort again.
reasons.hac: Fewer shifts mean fewer tankers of export ice.

answers.text: Let shift councils share out the cut.
answers.sub: Crews and blocks decide where the 8 percent falls.

reasons.riw: Those who make the air decide how it is shared.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks finally get a say over their own air.
reasons.hsd: Allocation handed to amateurs who cannot read a gauge.
reasons.aco: Councils over the meters weaken the chain of command.
reasons.mca: Geneva does not recognise union councils over life support.

answers.gripWhy: Allocation passes from the board to elected councils.

situations.title: Charter Blue Below Basalt
situations.question: Will you raise the Charter flag in every dome and swear the Constabulary?
situations.body: The inauguration directive came on the Geneva link. Charter blue in every dome, the tube included. The Constabulary's oath moves from the Directorate to the Charter. Dustline says any flag below the basalt line comes down by night.

answers.text: Fly the flags everywhere; swear the Constabulary in.
answers.sub: Charter oath in Dome 1; blue banners down the tube.

reasons.mca: The Charter's writ is visible in every dome.
reasons.aco: A clear chain of command straight up to Geneva.
reasons.fam: Earth flags in our tube are an occupation's banners.
reasons.hsd: Thirty years of Directorate command ended by one oath.
reasons.cas: The governor takes orders from Geneva, not the chamber.

answers.gripWhy: Officers sworn to Earth and flags guarded in the tube.

answers.text: Keep Earth flags out of the tube.
answers.sub: Charter blue in Domes 1 to 5 only.

reasons.fam: The tube stays ours, under the two moons.
reasons.cas: A governor who listens to the self-government bloc.
reasons.mca: A directive half obeyed is a precedent for secession.
reasons.aco: Officers ordered to leave the tube to the Areanists.

answers.text: Leave the oath with the Directorate.
answers.sub: The Constabulary keeps answering through the margin chain.

reasons.hsd: Security stays tied to the plants it protects.
reasons.upa: Geneva's grip on the Domes loosens a notch.
reasons.mca: The governor refuses the first order Geneva sends.
reasons.aco: We stay under engineers instead of the Charter.
reasons.fam: No oath to Earth is sworn over our heads.

situations.title: Air Sold Twice
situations.question: Will you tax the tube's air-credit market or let the Constabulary raid it?
situations.body: Resold air credits change hands at the Erebus Tube stalls for two to three times ration price. Chair Castellanos-Abe wants the trade licensed and levied. Constabulary officers have raided the stalls twice this quarter.

answers.text: License the air-credit trade and levy it.
answers.sub: Stalls register, brokers pay, the treasury gains.

reasons.lme: Our brokers trade in the open, with Charter paper.
reasons.hac: Priced air is a market the bondholders understand.
reasons.riw: Air we make is resold to us at triple price.
reasons.fam: Tube families now pay legal prices for their own air.
reasons.aco: Our raids become illegal and the stalls laugh at us.

answers.text: Raid the stalls under Charter ration law.
answers.sub: Credits seized, brokers fined, stalls shut.

reasons.aco: Order in the tube, and our officers backed.
reasons.mca: Charter ration law means what it says.
reasons.lme: Our members' stock seized by police at night.
reasons.fam: Constables kicking in stalls in our blocks again.

answers.gripWhy: Night raids on tube stalls by armed officers.

situations.title: The Edited Feed
situations.question: Will you let Assembly sittings run uncut on the Habitat Channel?
situations.body: Your office edits every Assembly broadcast before it reaches the domes. The self-government bloc and Free Arcadia want the feed live and whole. Last week's cut removed four minutes of the Speaker's levy speech.

answers.text: Run every sitting live and uncut.
answers.sub: No more edits; the chamber speaks to every dome.

reasons.cas: The chamber's words reach the settlers whole.
reasons.fam: Self-government speeches heard in every tube block.
reasons.lme: Our bench's levy fights get a public stage.
reasons.mca: Secession talk broadcast live under Charter authority.
reasons.aco: Live agitation on the channel stirs the tube.

answers.gripWhy: The governor gives up control of the broadcast.

answers.text: Keep the edit under Charter broadcast rules.
answers.sub: Your office still cuts the feed before release.

reasons.mca: No secessionist speeches carried on a Charter channel.
reasons.aco: Fewer slogans on screen, fewer at the locks.
reasons.cas: Our sittings censored by the governor's office.
reasons.fam: Dustline will carry what Dome 1 cuts.

answers.gripWhy: The governor keeps censoring the chamber.

situations.title: Dust in the Lungs
situations.question: Will you give union inspectors the power to stop a shift?
situations.body: There are 140 lung cases from Ice Field 7. Perchlorate dust gets past the suit seals. The RIWU wants its own medical inspectors, able to halt any shift. Helion-Ares says every halted shift is a lost tanker.

answers.text: Appoint RIWU inspectors who can halt shifts.
answers.sub: Union doctors walk the field with stop orders.

reasons.riw: Our own people decide when the dust is too thick.
reasons.fam: Mars-born crews protected by their own people.
reasons.hac: Quotas now hang on a union doctor's whim.
reasons.hsd: Shifts halted without regard to the margin board.
reasons.lme: Ice deliveries become unreliable for our contracts.

answers.text: Give Dr. Begić's service the inspection.
answers.sub: Directorate doctors certify suits; halts need Control Ring sign-off.

reasons.hsd: Certified staff, with halts weighed against the margins.
reasons.mca: Charter medical service keeps its authority.
reasons.hac: Fields keep running unless the engineers agree.
reasons.riw: The Directorate inspects itself while our lungs fill.

answers.text: Make Helion-Ares fund a compensation pool.
answers.sub: Sick crews get paid; quotas stay as they are.

reasons.hac: We pay for lungs on top of the quota.
reasons.lme: A paid settlement keeps the fields and trade moving.
reasons.riw: Money for the sick, though the dust stays.
reasons.cas: A deal the chamber can vote and claim.

situations.title: The Price of Six Months
situations.question: Will you trade exclusive ice export rights for the bond rollover?
situations.body: The ₵1.2 billion tranche comes due in October. The treasury holds ₵2.4 billion and loses ₵150M a month. Chief Executive Sørlie-Tan offers six more months at 9 percent. Her price: exclusive rights to export Arcadian ice.

answers.text: Grant Helion-Ares the exclusive export rights.
answers.sub: The bond rolls over; every tonne leaves on their hulls.

reasons.hac: Bonds serviced and the ice trade locked up.
reasons.lme: Stable credit and cargo work for the arcade.
reasons.upa: Utopia is shut out of Arcadian ice.
reasons.riw: Our ice sold abroad by the company that sets quotas.
reasons.fam: Arcadia's ice signed away to an Earth corporation.

answers.text: Refuse; Arcadian ice stays Arcadian.
answers.sub: No monopoly; the tranche must be found elsewhere.

reasons.fam: The colony keeps its ice and its future.
reasons.cas: The ice stays a matter for the chamber.
reasons.upa: The door to an ice lease stays open.
reasons.hac: Our bonds left hanging over a refusal.
reasons.lme: Credit tightens with the bondholders angry.

situations.title: The Citizenship Line
situations.question: Will you enforce the Charter's new roll on Mars-born families?
situations.body: Geneva wants every Mars-born child entered as an Earth citizen. Registrars sit in Dome 1 and the Erebus concourse. Free Arcadia block committees tell families not to register. On day three, 212 forms were filed for 11,400 Mars-born.

answers.text: Tie ration cards to registration.
answers.sub: No roll entry, no card; registrars backed by officers.

reasons.mca: Every Mars-born on the roll as an Earth citizen.
reasons.aco: A full roll makes the tube knowable.
reasons.fam: Air held hostage to a leash from Geneva.
reasons.cas: Coercion on the roll without one Assembly vote.
reasons.riw: Our members' families threatened through their rations.

answers.gripWhy: Rations become leverage for compulsory registration.

answers.text: Record the Mars-born as Arcadians, not Earth citizens.
answers.sub: A colony roll with no citizenship line for Geneva.

reasons.fam: The governor writes our people down as Arcadians.
reasons.cas: A colonial roll the chamber can own.
reasons.mca: The governor defies the Charter on citizenship itself.
reasons.aco: Our oath is to a Charter the governor now ignores.

answers.text: Let block committees count heads, no citizenship.
answers.sub: Workplace and block lists for rations only.

reasons.riw: Our committees, not Geneva's clerks, hold the lists.
reasons.fam: Counted for air, never for Earth.
reasons.hsd: An accurate headcount for the ration tables.
reasons.mca: Geneva's roll replaced by union lists.
reasons.aco: Committees hold records that police cannot see.

situations.title: Nine Private Decks
situations.question: Will you seize the Exchange's greenhouse decks for the calorie plan?
situations.body: Storm season is five months out. Exchange families run nine private greenhouse decks in Dome 2. The Directorate wants their yield in the common calorie plan. Chair Castellanos-Abe calls requisition theft.

answers.text: Requisition the decks into the calorie plan.
answers.sub: Directorate planners run the yield from next sol.

reasons.hsd: Every calorie counted before the storm hits.
reasons.riw: Private decks feed everyone, not only the rich.
reasons.upa: A planned colony is a colony we can deal with.
reasons.lme: Confiscation of our decks crosses our red line.
reasons.hac: Private property seized; investors watch nervously.

answers.gripWhy: Private decks taken by order.

answers.text: Buy their surplus at market price.
answers.sub: Treasury pays; decks stay private.

reasons.lme: Our harvest sells at a fair price.
reasons.hac: Property respected even before a storm.
reasons.hsd: Calories at market prices wreck the plan.
reasons.riw: Public credits flow to deck owners.

answers.text: Hand the decks to RIWU hydroponics crews.
answers.sub: Crews run them as common stock.

reasons.riw: The decks go to those who grow the food.
reasons.fam: Food for the tube, out of merchant hands.
reasons.lme: Our decks handed to the union outright.
reasons.hac: Expropriation today, the ice plant tomorrow.
reasons.aco: Union crews holding decks the Charter calls private.

situations.title: Areography Lessons
situations.question: Will you replace the Earth syllabus with an Arcadian curriculum?
situations.body: Schools still teach Earth geography and Concord civics. Mars-born teachers have written an Arcadian history and areography course. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau objects on the Geneva link. About 4,000 pupils start the next term.

answers.text: Adopt the Arcadian curriculum this term.
answers.sub: Sols, basalt, Arcadia's history; Concord civics dropped.

reasons.fam: Our children learn they are a people.
reasons.cas: The chamber's bloc wins its first real reform.
reasons.mca: A generation schooled for secession on our subsidy.
reasons.aco: The schools raise the next Pressure Cells.

answers.text: Keep the Concord syllabus and Earth exams.
answers.sub: Earth certificates stay valid for return passage.

reasons.mca: Mars-born children stay Concord citizens in mind.
reasons.aco: Order begins with what children are taught.
reasons.fam: Our children taught a planet they will never see.
reasons.cas: The governor overrules the teachers and the chamber.

situations.title: One Shift to Answer
situations.question: The crews walk out next shift. Whose side will you take, Governor?
situations.body: Helion-Ares raised Ice Field 7 quotas by 15 percent. The RIWU voted a 72-hour stoppage by raised gloves. Kamau-Quispe gave you one shift. The tankers feed the water reserve, now 240 days.

answers.text: Order Helion-Ares to freeze the quota rise
answers.sub: Quotas return to the old rate. Crews stay on shift.

reasons.riw: The quota falls without a single lost shift.
reasons.hac: A governor rewriting our contract terms threatens every bond.
reasons.lme: Ice costs rise and the merchants pay the gap.
reasons.hsd: Tankers keep running and the water margin holds.
reasons.fam: Geneva's governor bending to Arcadian hands is a start.

answers.text: Back the Consortium quota and dock strike pay
answers.sub: The 15 percent stands. Strikers lose their shift credits.

reasons.hac: Our contract holds and the bondholders see a firm hand.
reasons.lme: Export volume keeps the arcade's credit lines open.
reasons.riw: Docking pay for lung-burned crews is open war.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice dug harder for Earth's bondholders.
reasons.hsd: A stoppage now drains the water reserve.

answers.text: Post Constabulary to keep the tankers rolling
answers.sub: Officers escort tanker crews past any picket line.
answers.gripWhy: Armed officers guard the ice routes against a union.

reasons.aco: Charter order on the ice routes, under our command.
reasons.mca: Charter law keeps the colony's water flowing.
reasons.riw: Armed police on the fields is our red line.
reasons.cas: The Assembly was not even consulted on armed escorts.
reasons.hac: The tankers move and our shipments leave on time.

situations.title: Stacks from the West
situations.question: Director Wen's stacks are ready to roll. Will you sell Utopia your ice?
situations.body: Utopia Planitia offers new electrolysis stacks for 600 tonnes of Arcadian ice a year. Director Wen also wants a liaison office in the Domes. Helion-Ares holds export claims on that ice. Oxygen sits near the 180-day floor.

answers.text: Take the stacks and ship 600 tonnes
answers.sub: Utopian hardware in the plants. A liaison office opens.

reasons.upa: Ice, a foothold in the Domes, and Geneva's grip loosened.
reasons.hsd: New stacks lift the oxygen margin off the floor.
reasons.hac: Our export claims cut in half by a rival state.
reasons.mca: A Utopian office in a Charter settlement sets a precedent.
reasons.riw: More stacks mean fewer forced shifts in the halls.

answers.text: Refuse and honour Helion-Ares export claims
answers.sub: Every tonne stays on the Consortium's contract books.

reasons.hac: The governor respects contracts. The bonds stay safe.
reasons.lme: Consortium cargo slots keep the merchants' trade alive.
reasons.upa: Arcadia chooses an Earth company over its neighbour.
reasons.hsd: The plants go on without the stacks they need.

answers.text: Refer the offer to Geneva for ruling
answers.sub: Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau decides. Months pass on the link.

reasons.mca: Foreign deals belong to the Charter Authority.
reasons.aco: The chain of command runs to Geneva, as it should.
reasons.upa: Geneva's answer is already known. Our offer dies.
reasons.hsd: The margins cannot wait on Geneva's delay.
reasons.cas: Arcadia's ice is decided in Geneva again.

situations.title: Air Is Ours
situations.question: Every tube lock says 'Air Is Ours'. Will you post officers there permanently?
situations.body: The slogan appeared overnight on every Free Arcadia-district lock door. Commandant Osei-Brandt asks for permanent posts in the Erebus Tube concourse. Duct-drums beat the sol rhythm under the basalt galleries.

answers.text: Station permanent posts in the concourse
answers.sub: Officers on every shift at the Erebus Tube locks.
answers.gripWhy: A standing police presence over the Mars-born districts.

reasons.aco: The tube is held. Officers own the locks again.
reasons.mca: Charter authority visible where it is most defied.
reasons.fam: An occupation of our own concourse.
reasons.cas: Policing tube voters will cost the Assembly their trust.
reasons.lme: Quieter concourse, safer stalls for the arcade trade.

answers.text: Let tube block committees scrub the doors
answers.sub: Residents police their own locks. No new posts.
answers.gripWhy: The Mars-born police their own districts.

reasons.fam: Our committees, recognised by Dome 1 in all but name.
reasons.cas: Local self-rule is the Assembly's own argument.
reasons.aco: Handing the locks to Free Arcadia's own committees.
reasons.mca: Graffiti answered with concessions invites worse.

situations.title: Fees at the Pads
situations.question: The Pad Field earns nothing. Will you let the Exchange charge every lander?
situations.body: The Exchange and Helion-Ares propose a for-profit pad concession at the Pad Field. Utopian rovers and Charter ships alike would pay a landing fee. The treasury loses ₵150M a month.

answers.text: Grant the pad concession to Exchange and Helion
answers.sub: Private operators charge every ship. The treasury takes a share.

reasons.lme: The pads become profit for the Exchange families.
reasons.hac: Our cargo flows through gates we co-own.
reasons.upa: Fees on our convoys from a Consortium tollbooth.
reasons.mca: Charter ships paying private tolls is unseemly.
reasons.hsd: Pad power and scheduling leave Directorate control.

answers.text: Keep the pads under Directorate control at cost
answers.sub: Landings are scheduled by margin, not by price.

reasons.hsd: Landing slots stay tied to power and safety margins.
reasons.upa: Our convoys land on engineering terms, not tolls.
reasons.lme: Another revenue stream locked up by engineers.
reasons.hac: Consortium cargo waits on a Directorate schedule.

answers.text: Free pads for Arcadian craft, fees on Earth ships
answers.sub: Local landers fly free. Earth shippers pay the treasury.

reasons.fam: Arcadian ground, Arcadian rules at the gate.
reasons.cas: The colony sets its own duties at last.
reasons.mca: Taxing Charter ships is a customs border with Earth.
reasons.hac: Our ships pay for Areanist symbolism.
reasons.lme: Local trade flies free, and local merchants gain.

situations.title: Close the Airlock
situations.question: Valdivia told the tube to close the airlock on Geneva. Will you sign?
situations.body: Ezra Valdivia, 27, broadcast 'close the airlock on Geneva' on the Dustline. The Constabulary asks for a warrant under Charter Article 19 for sedition. The broadcast reached every Free Arcadia block.

answers.text: Sign the Article 19 sedition warrant
answers.sub: Valdivia is detained tonight and held for trial.
answers.gripWhy: The movement's founder jailed for a broadcast.

reasons.aco: Sedition met with Charter law. Our authority stands.
reasons.mca: Secession talk is answered before it spreads.
reasons.fam: Our founder jailed for words is a declaration of war.
reasons.cas: Arresting a speaker chills every Assembly debate.
reasons.riw: Today Valdivia, tomorrow the union's stewards.

answers.text: Refuse: it was speech, not sedition
answers.sub: No warrant. Valdivia keeps broadcasting.
answers.gripWhy: Arcadian political speech is left unpunished.

reasons.fam: The governor admits Arcadians may speak of freedom.
reasons.cas: Free speech protects every bench in the chamber.
reasons.aco: A soft governor lets the Pressure Cells grow.
reasons.mca: Geneva sees a governor shielding a secessionist.

answers.text: Pull his feed off the relays, no arrest
answers.sub: The Directorate cuts his signal on relay-load grounds.
answers.gripWhy: A broadcast silenced by engineering order.

reasons.hsd: Relay capacity is a systems matter, rightly ours.
reasons.aco: The signal is down without a martyr.
reasons.fam: Censorship dressed up as a load report.
reasons.cas: Engineers deciding who may broadcast is dangerous.
reasons.mca: Sedition goes unpunished behind a technicality.

situations.title: Deck 4 Council
situations.question: The crews grow Deck 4's calories. Will you let their council run it?
situations.body: Hydroponics crews ask to run Greenhouse Deck 4 as a cooperative. An elected RIWU council would set planting and shares. It would leave the Directorate's calorie plan.

answers.text: Charter Deck 4 to an elected RIWU council
answers.sub: Crews plant and share by council vote.

reasons.riw: The first deck held in common by its workers.
reasons.fam: Arcadian hands feeding Arcadians, no Geneva in between.
reasons.hsd: A hole in the calorie plan before storm season.
reasons.lme: Today one deck goes to councils, tomorrow ours.

answers.text: Keep Deck 4 under the calorie plan
answers.sub: The Directorate sets planting. Crews work to schedule.

reasons.hsd: One calorie plan, one set of margins.
reasons.hac: Union councils stay out of colony assets.
reasons.riw: The decks stay the engineers', the work stays ours.
reasons.fam: The Directorate still rations what Arcadians grow.

situations.title: Retire Dome 3
situations.question: Dome 3 bleeds air every sol. Will you empty it?
situations.body: Dome 3 leaks 0.4 percent of its air a sol. The Directorate wants to retire it and move 2,100 residents into the lava tube. The Assembly members for Dome 3 refuse to vote for it.

answers.text: Retire Dome 3 and move 2,100 into the tube
answers.sub: Dome 3 is sealed off. Residents relocate within 30 sols.

reasons.hsd: The worst leak in the colony stops for good.
reasons.fam: Two thousand more settlers under Arcadian basalt.
reasons.cas: Our members' constituents uprooted by engineering fiat.
reasons.aco: Two thousand angry movers crowd the tube.

answers.text: Lease the resealing to Exchange contractors
answers.sub: Private crews reseal Dome 3 on a paid contract.

reasons.lme: A public contract paid to Exchange fabrication shops.
reasons.hac: Our sealant stock sells at full price.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified crews patching a dome we condemned.
reasons.riw: Hab maintenance work handed to private crews.
reasons.cas: Dome 3's residents keep their homes.

answers.text: Ask Geneva for a Dome 3 sealant grant
answers.sub: Earth pays for sealant. Repairs wait for the fleet.

reasons.mca: The colony turns to Geneva for rescue, as intended.
reasons.cas: Residents stay put and the Assembly is heard.
reasons.hsd: The leak continues for months awaiting Earth cargo.
reasons.aco: Charter channels, Charter order.

situations.title: Geneva Auditors
situations.question: The auditors want every ledger and raw margin. Will you open them?
situations.body: A Charter Authority audit team asks for the Assembly's levy accounts. It also wants the Directorate's raw margin data. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran and Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist both call it Geneva spying.

answers.text: Open both ledgers to the Geneva auditors
answers.sub: Full access to levy books and raw margin logs.

reasons.mca: The Charter's trustee sees what it underwrites.
reasons.aco: Charter oversight keeps everyone honest.
reasons.cas: Geneva's clerks reading our levy votes line by line.
reasons.hsd: Our raw data second-guessed by non-engineers.
reasons.fam: Proof the colony is still Geneva's property.

answers.text: Close the books: Arcadia audits itself
answers.sub: Auditors get summaries only. Local auditors keep the ledgers.

reasons.cas: The levy belongs to the chamber that votes it.
reasons.fam: A governor closing the door on Geneva.
reasons.hsd: Our margin data stays with those who certify it.
reasons.mca: Refusing a Charter audit is defiance of the Charter.
reasons.hac: Bondholders lose a clean Earth audit of the colony.

situations.title: Storm Rationing Powers
situations.question: The storm drops the forecast to 150 days. Will you override the Assembly?
situations.body: The dust storm is forecast. The oxygen forecast falls to 150 days, below the 180-day floor. The Directorate asks for rationing powers over the Assembly for the storm's length. The three-tone chime opened the margin reading.

answers.text: Grant storm rationing powers over the Assembly
answers.sub: The Directorate sets air and power rations by order.
answers.gripWhy: Rationing by decree, past the elected Assembly.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, not the floor of a chamber.
reasons.mca: A firm hand through the storm.
reasons.cas: Our vote over rations suspended by engineers.
reasons.riw: Rations cut from above, shift crews hit first.
reasons.lme: Power cuts land on private shops first.

answers.text: Let block and shift councils share the ration
answers.sub: Elected councils divide each dome's air and power quota.
answers.gripWhy: Rationing handed to elected councils.

reasons.riw: The common stock shared by those who produce it.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks run their own air at last.
reasons.hsd: Fifty councils guessing at margins in a storm.
reasons.aco: No clear chain of command through the storm.
reasons.lme: Councils will ration the arcade before the blocks.

answers.text: Price surplus air through tradeable credits
answers.sub: Base rations stay. Extra air trades on the Exchange.

reasons.lme: Air credits become a legal market, and ours.
reasons.hac: Scarcity priced properly, as it should be.
reasons.riw: Crews who make the air must buy it back.
reasons.fam: Earth money buys Arcadian breath.
reasons.hsd: Prices are no substitute for a margin plan.

situations.title: Shelters for a Holiday
situations.question: The Exchange builds three tube shelters. Will you waive its levy two years?
situations.body: The Exchange offers to fund three storm shelters in the Erebus Tube. In return its members want a two-year levy holiday. Treasury income from the levy would fall.

answers.text: Take the shelters, grant the levy holiday
answers.sub: Three shelters open. Exchange trade pays no levy.

reasons.lme: Two levy-free years for three shelters is a bargain.
reasons.hac: A governor who rewards private investment.
reasons.cas: The levy is ours to vote, not yours to waive.
reasons.riw: Merchants pay nothing while crews pay full levy.
reasons.fam: Shelters in the tube, wherever the credits come from.

answers.text: Raise a levy and let union crews build
answers.sub: RIWU maintenance gangs build the shelters on public pay.

reasons.riw: Paid shelter work for union gangs.
reasons.fam: The tube built by its own people.
reasons.lme: A new levy to pay the union's wages.
reasons.cas: A levy raised without a full chamber debate.

situations.title: Concourse for Pressure Day
situations.question: Governor, will you give your concourse to Pressure Day?
situations.body: Valdivia sits in a Dome 1 cell under Article 19. Free Arcadia wants the Erebus concourse for one sol. Major Novak-Sato says 6,000 bodies would choke three emergency locks. 'Air Is Ours' is already stencilled on the gates.

answers.text: Grant the concourse for a full sol
answers.sub: Block marshals run it; Constabulary watches from the locks.

reasons.fam: The tube sees the Mars-born can gather openly.
reasons.cas: The self-government bloc rides the crowd's energy.
reasons.riw: Union youth march with their neighbours.
reasons.aco: Six thousand bodies at three locks, and we stand aside.
reasons.mca: A sedition suspect's rally licensed by Geneva's own governor.

answers.gripWhy: A banned movement gets the colony's biggest hall.

answers.text: Ban the rally under lock-safety rules
answers.sub: Concourse sealed; Constabulary holds the gates for the sol.

reasons.aco: The locks stay ours and the crowd stays home.
reasons.mca: Charter safety law applied without blinking.
reasons.hsd: No crush loads on the emergency locks.
reasons.fam: Valdivia jailed and his people locked out too.
reasons.cas: Members' constituents banned from their own concourse.

answers.gripWhy: The concourse is sealed by Constabulary order.

answers.text: Move it to the Ice Field 7 hall
answers.sub: Union stewards host; the rally becomes a joint meeting.

reasons.riw: Our hall, our stewards, our voice in the movement.
reasons.aco: Out of the concourse, away from the main locks.
reasons.fam: The union takes our day and our crowd.
reasons.hsd: Politics packed beside the electrolysis feed lines.
reasons.hac: A strike hall turned into a protest hall.

situations.title: Passage for the Frail

carrier.name: Amara Begić
carrier.role: Chief Medical Officer of Ares Landing

situations.question: Will you pay passage home for 300 frail settlers, Governor?
situations.body: Dr. Begić lists 300 settlers over 70 or with failing lungs. The Charter would pay their berths on the return leg. Each one off the roll eases the air. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran's bloc calls it a cull dressed as medicine.

answers.text: Accept Charter-paid passage, strictly voluntary
answers.sub: Geneva pays berths; Medical Service certifies each consent.

reasons.mca: The rescue guarantee shown working for Earth citizens.
reasons.hsd: Three hundred fewer draws on a thin oxygen margin.
reasons.aco: Families with Earth pensions see Geneva keep faith.
reasons.cas: Our old shipped off the roll before the vote.
reasons.fam: Geneva thins the roll and calls it care.

answers.text: Refuse; Arcadia cares for its own old
answers.sub: No return berths; the colony carries its frail.

reasons.fam: Arcadians do not send their elders away.
reasons.cas: The roll stays whole and the chamber is heard.
reasons.mca: Refusing Charter rescue sets a dangerous precedent.
reasons.hsd: Three hundred more on a reserve near the floor.

answers.text: Let families buy berths through the Exchange
answers.sub: Passage sold at cost; the Exchange brokers seats.

reasons.lme: Brokerage fees and a new passage market.
reasons.hac: Return-leg berths sell through our slots.
reasons.riw: Only the rich get a ticket home.
reasons.cas: Rescue priced like cargo insults every member.
reasons.mca: Charter rescue is a right, not a sale.

situations.title: A Seat for Full Shifts
situations.question: Will you seat the union on the allocation board for full shifts?
situations.body: The 72-hour stoppage ended. Work-to-rule did not. Ice deliveries run 20 percent short. Kamau-Quispe's price: one permanent RIWU vote on the Directorate allocation board. Dr. Haddad-Lindqvist says votes do not belong beside gauges.

answers.text: Give the RIWU a permanent board seat
answers.sub: One union vote on every power, air and water allocation.

reasons.riw: The ones who mine the ice now share it out.
reasons.fam: Tube workers gain a hand on the air.
reasons.hsd: A union vote over certified margins.
reasons.hac: Our quotas now answer to the crews.
reasons.lme: Union hands on the power we buy.

answers.gripWhy: Allocation opens to an elected union voice.

answers.text: Keep the board certified engineers only
answers.sub: Union gets read access to margins, no vote.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide, not the picket line.
reasons.hac: Quotas stay with management and engineers.
reasons.upa: A board run by engineers is one Utopia trusts.
reasons.riw: Work-to-rule continues until the board opens.
reasons.cas: No elected voice on the board, again.

answers.text: Pay a delivery bonus to end work-to-rule
answers.sub: Treasury and Helion-Ares fund per-tonne bonuses.

reasons.riw: Pay in hand, though the board stays shut.
reasons.hac: Tonnage restored without giving up control.
reasons.lme: Ice flows and trade runs again.
reasons.hsd: Buying shifts leaves the next stoppage unsolved.
reasons.cas: Levy money spent without our vote.

situations.title: Asking for Marines
situations.question: Will you formally ask Geneva for a battalion of Charter Marines?
situations.body: Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau's cable is short: ask, and 400 Marines sail with the Window Fleet. Do not ask, and Geneva notes it. The Constabulary has 600 officers. Dustline already calls any request an invasion order.

answers.text: Sign the request for 400 Marines
answers.sub: A battalion sails with the fleet under Charter command.

reasons.mca: The governor invites Charter force: secession is answered.
reasons.hac: Marines protect bonds and plants alike.
reasons.aco: Marines could take our posts and our budget line.
reasons.fam: The governor sent for Earth's guns.
reasons.upa: A Marine battalion a few thousand km east.
reasons.cas: Troops requested without a word to the chamber.

answers.gripWhy: Earth troops invited to back your writ.

answers.text: Decline; Arcadia keeps its own peace
answers.sub: No request filed; security stays local.

reasons.fam: No soldiers sent for against the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: The chamber's warning heeded.
reasons.aco: No Marine officers over our heads.
reasons.mca: Refusing Charter protection smells of separatism.
reasons.hac: Our plants stay guarded by 600 police.

answers.text: Ask for engineers and spares instead
answers.sub: Fleet berths go to reactor crews and electrolysis stacks.

reasons.hsd: Berths for stacks and crews, not rifles.
reasons.upa: No Marines pointed west.
reasons.mca: Geneva offered security; the governor bargains.
reasons.aco: Reinforcement refused while the tube simmers.
reasons.riw: Earth crews in the halls undercut union shifts.

situations.title: Dark Shops, Live Air
situations.question: Will you shut the Exchange fab shops to feed the air plants?
situations.body: Solar output stands at 60 percent. The fabrication shops along the Pad Field draw 9 percent of colony power. The Directorate wants them dark until the dust clears. Chair Castellanos-Abe says 400 contracts die with them.

answers.text: Shut the shops; power to the air plants
answers.sub: Fab lines dark for the storm; load goes to electrolysis.

reasons.hsd: Every spare kilowatt holds the oxygen margin.
reasons.riw: Electrolysis crews get steady load.
reasons.mca: Air before commerce, as the Charter demands.
reasons.lme: Four hundred contracts dead by decree.
reasons.hac: Our fabrication orders stall for 51 sols.

answers.gripWhy: Private shops closed by Directorate order.

answers.text: Keep shops open; Exchange buys its own cells
answers.sub: Shops run on imported cells billed to owners.

reasons.lme: Trade survives the storm on our own coin.
reasons.hac: Cell sales and fab orders both continue.
reasons.cas: Members' businesses spared a shutdown.
reasons.hsd: Load risk left in merchant hands.
reasons.riw: Shops hum while hall shifts get cut.

answers.text: Shops run at night under union power quotas
answers.sub: Shift councils ration shop power hour by hour.

reasons.riw: Workers decide who draws power and when.
reasons.fam: Councils over Exchange owners suits the tube.
reasons.lme: Union clerks rationing our machines.
reasons.hsd: Councils guessing at load curves.
reasons.hac: Our contractors bow to shift councils.

situations.title: Cells at Any Price
situations.question: Whose power cells will you buy to ride out the storm?
situations.body: Helion-Ares offers 80 emergency cells at three times the contract price, paid now. Director Wen offers cheaper cells by rover, with twelve Utopian technicians to install them. The treasury already loses ₵150M a month.

answers.text: Pay Helion-Ares the triple price
answers.sub: Cells land on contract; the Consortium keeps its monopoly.

reasons.hac: Storm margins at triple price, contract intact.
reasons.lme: Earth supply lines stay open for trade.
reasons.upa: Our offer spurned for the monopoly.
reasons.riw: Ice money poured into Consortium profit.
reasons.cas: The levy drained without debate.

answers.text: Take Utopia's cells and technicians
answers.sub: Twelve Utopian engineers work inside the Control Ring.

reasons.upa: Our people inside Arcadia's plants at last.
reasons.hsd: Cheaper cells, competent hands, margin saved.
reasons.hac: Our supply monopoly broken mid-storm.
reasons.mca: Utopian crews inside a Charter colony's plants.
reasons.aco: Foreign technicians behind our lock codes.

answers.text: Build cells in the tube workshops
answers.sub: Mars-born fabricators improvise from salvage: slower, ours.

reasons.fam: Arcadian hands keep Arcadian lights on.
reasons.lme: Tube shops win the salvage contracts.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified cells on certified circuits.
reasons.hac: The colony learns to do without us.
reasons.upa: Arcadia leans on neither neighbour.

situations.title: The Bond's Second Price
situations.question: Will you give Helion-Ares a board seat to roll the bond?
situations.body: The ₵1.2 billion tranche needs rolling. Helion-Ares now wants more than ice rights: a voting seat on the Directorate board and a cap on the Assembly's levy power. Dust still blankets the solar fields. The Speaker calls it a mortgage on the chamber.

answers.text: Grant the seat and the levy cap
answers.sub: Bond rolls; the Consortium votes on margins; levy capped.

reasons.hac: Our bonds now sit beside the margins.
reasons.lme: Capped levies mean lighter trade taxes.
reasons.cas: The levy is our one real power.
reasons.hsd: A bondholder voting on air allocation.
reasons.riw: The Consortium now votes on our quotas.

answers.text: Refuse; put the plant under worker audit
answers.sub: Union auditors open the Consortium's ice-plant books.

reasons.riw: The books that set our quotas, opened.
reasons.fam: Earth capital told no in the tube's name.
reasons.hac: Union auditors on our plant: a red line.
reasons.lme: Credit dries up when creditors are audited.
reasons.mca: A Charter colony provoking its bondholders.

answers.text: Ask Geneva to guarantee the rollover
answers.sub: The Charter Authority underwrites; terms set from Geneva.

reasons.mca: The colony's debt runs through Geneva again.
reasons.aco: Charter chain of command holds firm.
reasons.hac: Geneva's terms are softer than ours.
reasons.cas: Our finances handed back to Earth.
reasons.fam: Another Earth leash on Arcadian ice.

situations.title: Reactor Two Runs Hot
situations.question: Will you take Reactor Two down now, or run it hot?
situations.body: Reactor Two's coolant loop reads 14 degrees over limit. Repair needs 30 sols offline. Utopian crews could cut that to 20. Running it keeps the storm-season lights on, until it scrams.

answers.text: Take it down; repair with Utopian crews
answers.sub: Outage and rationed power; Utopian crews in the vault.

reasons.hsd: A planned outage beats an unplanned scram.
reasons.upa: Our engineers inside Arcadia's reactor.
reasons.lme: Rationed power during the storm guts trade.
reasons.hac: Utopians on a reactor we built.
reasons.mca: Utopian hands on a Charter reactor.

answers.gripWhy: Power rationed by decree for the repair.

answers.text: Run it hot; keep the shops powered
answers.sub: Full load to the domes; repair after the storm.

reasons.lme: Shops and arcade stay lit through the dust.
reasons.hac: No Utopian crews, contracts keep running.
reasons.hsd: Gambling the colony's power on a failing loop.
reasons.riw: Our operators stand beside an overheating vault.
reasons.upa: Our help refused for a dangerous bet.

situations.title: The Tube Watches
situations.question: Will you let the Tube Watches patrol your lava tube?
situations.body: Two hundred Mars-born under 25 wear rust armbands and walk the tube terraces at night. They want lawful standing in place of Constabulary posts. Commandant Osei-Brandt calls them Free Arcadia's militia. Pressure Cell tags appear near their muster point.

answers.text: Deputise the Watches for tube districts
answers.sub: Armbands become lawful; Constabulary leaves the inner terraces.

reasons.fam: Arcadians policing Arcadia: the first step to self-rule.
reasons.cas: Local policing under local faces.
reasons.aco: A Free Arcadia militia given our posts.
reasons.mca: A separatist force with a Charter warrant.
reasons.lme: Who protects arcade stock from armbands?

answers.gripWhy: Policing handed to the tube's own youth.

answers.text: Disband them; Constabulary holds the tube
answers.sub: Armbands banned; patrols doubled under Major Novak-Sato.

reasons.aco: One armed service in the tube: ours.
reasons.mca: No militia under the Charter.
reasons.fam: Youth banned and patrolled: they go to the Cells.
reasons.cas: Doubled patrols in members' districts.
reasons.riw: More police near the halls and picket lines.

answers.gripWhy: Armbands banned and patrols doubled.

answers.text: Fold them into union block wardens
answers.sub: RIWU wardens train them; no arms, shift rosters.

reasons.riw: Youth on union rosters, not militia rolls.
reasons.hsd: Trained wardens on lock and leak watch.
reasons.fam: Our Watches absorbed by the union.
reasons.aco: Union wardens doing police work.
reasons.hac: The union grows a street arm.

situations.title: Inquiry Into Train 3
situations.question: Governor, will you let union investigators into Train 3?
situations.body: Sabatier Train 3 burned at shift change. Two operators are dead. Methane and water recovery is down 30 percent. The Directorate has sealed the hall for a closed review. Ice Field 7 crews wear black tape on their gloves.

answers.text: Order a public joint inquiry with RIWU investigators
answers.sub: Union investigators read the logs; hearings run on the Channel.

reasons.riw: Our own people finally read the logs that killed ours.
reasons.hsd: Untrained union eyes in a sealed plant, second-guessing certifications.
reasons.hac: Public hearings put our quota pressure on the record.
reasons.cas: Open hearings give the Assembly a seat at the table.
reasons.aco: Union investigators in a sealed hall undercut lock discipline.

answers.gripWhy: A public inquiry opens Directorate records to the street.

answers.text: Keep the closed Directorate review
answers.sub: Certified engineers only; findings released once the train is safe.

reasons.riw: Two of ours dead and the bosses grade their own work.
reasons.hsd: Engineers judge engineering. The plant stays ours to fix.
reasons.hac: A closed review keeps quotas out of the findings.
reasons.fam: Geneva's engineers bury Mars-born dead behind sealed doors.
reasons.upa: A disciplined technical bureau is the partner we prefer.

answers.gripWhy: The findings stay sealed inside the Control Ring.

answers.text: Hand it to a Charter inspector on Geneva link
answers.sub: Earth safety law applies; findings go to Geneva first.

reasons.mca: Charter law reaches the plants, as the Charter intends.
reasons.hsd: Earth clerks twenty minutes away grading our trains.
reasons.aco: Earth law and a clear chain up to Geneva.
reasons.riw: Geneva's inspector answers to Geneva, not to the crews.
reasons.cas: The Assembly is cut out again in favour of Earth.

situations.title: Who Judges Valdivia
situations.question: Governor, who will you let judge Ezra Valdivia?
situations.body: Valdivia's trial opens next sol. Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran wants twelve settler jurors. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau wants a Charter judge on the Geneva link, twenty minutes' signal lag. The tube has chalked the trial date on every lock.

answers.text: Seat a jury of twelve settlers
answers.sub: Arcadians judge an Arcadian; Geneva watches from the link.

reasons.fam: Ezra faces his own people, not a screen from Earth.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's demand carried; settlers sit in judgement.
reasons.mca: A colonial jury for sedition is a secession precedent.
reasons.aco: Tube jurors will free the man who called for this.
reasons.upa: Every crack in Geneva's writ serves the west.

answers.gripWhy: Justice passes from Charter judges to settler jurors.

answers.text: Let the Charter judge sit alone
answers.sub: Sedition is a Charter offence; Geneva's bench decides it.

reasons.mca: Charter crimes are judged by the Charter. No exceptions.
reasons.aco: Our arrest stands before a judge who will convict.
reasons.fam: An Earth screen sentencing a Mars-born. That is occupation.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's motion for a jury is simply ignored.
reasons.lme: A show trial means riots, and riots close the arcade.

answers.gripWhy: Geneva's bench overrides the settlers' claim to judge.

answers.text: Hire a neutral Earth arbitration bench
answers.sub: Exchange-funded jurists; costly, but neither Geneva's nor the tube's.

reasons.lme: A paid bench is calm, and calm sells.
reasons.hac: Commercial arbiters are a precedent our contracts welcome.
reasons.mca: Sedition farmed out to hired lawyers. Charter justice sold.
reasons.fam: Bought judges are still Earth's judges.
reasons.cas: The Assembly asked for settlers and got contractors.

situations.title: The Price of Spares
situations.question: Governor, what will you give Utopia for these spares?
situations.body: Fourteen rovers stand at the Pad Field gates. Forty tonnes of electrolysis spares, hauled 3,800 km overland. Director Wen asks a lease on Ice Field 9 and a Utopian crew in the Control Ring. Helion-Ares calls Field 9 its export claim.

answers.text: Seat a Utopian crew under Directorate certification
answers.sub: Utopian technicians work the stacks, under Haddad-Lindqvist's sign-off.

reasons.upa: Our engineers inside the Ring. That is the foothold we wanted.
reasons.hsd: Skilled hands on the stacks, certified to our standard.
reasons.hac: Utopian crews beside our plant, eyeing our ice.
reasons.mca: A rival state inside the Charter's life-support bureau.
reasons.aco: Foreign technicians behind Directorate locks we cannot inspect.

answers.text: Pay for the spares in credits, no lease
answers.sub: Buy the forty tonnes outright; Field 9 stays Helion-Ares's claim.

reasons.hac: Our export claim is honoured. Business stays business.
reasons.lme: A cash deal, no strings. The way trade should run.
reasons.upa: Credits are not influence. Wen wanted a foothold.
reasons.hsd: Spares on the stacks, whoever pays for them.

answers.text: Lease Field 9 to Utopia, without Geneva
answers.sub: A colony-to-colony deal, signed in the Domes, not Geneva.

reasons.upa: Arcadia signs with its neighbour directly. Geneva is bypassed.
reasons.fam: Arcadian ice, leased by Arcadians, to whom we choose.
reasons.mca: A treaty without the Charter. That is secession.
reasons.hac: Our export claim handed to a state rival.
reasons.aco: Utopian crews on an ice field we must now police.

situations.title: Jamming Dustline
situations.question: Governor, will you sign the order to jam Dustline?
situations.body: Dustline reaches every Free Arcadia block from a mobile transmitter. Mira Solheim reads Valdivia's letters nightly. Commandant Osei-Brandt wants taps on the Habitat Channel and jammers on the tube relays.

answers.text: Authorise monitoring and jam Dustline
answers.sub: Constabulary taps the Channel; jammers on every tube relay.

reasons.aco: Sedition off the air, and our officers finally hear the tube.
reasons.mca: Seditious broadcasts silenced under Charter emergency law.
reasons.fam: They want to cut the voice of the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: Taps on the Channel will reach the Assembly's own sittings.
reasons.lme: Jammers on the relays scramble arcade traffic too.

answers.gripWhy: State surveillance of the colony's one channel.

answers.text: Refuse; Dustline stays on the air
answers.sub: No taps, no jammers; the Channel stays unwatched.

reasons.fam: Mira keeps reading. The tube keeps listening.
reasons.cas: No one taps the Channel the Assembly speaks on.
reasons.aco: Seditionists broadcast freely and we patrol blind.
reasons.mca: The governor shelters a separatist transmitter.
reasons.upa: Loud Areanists keep Geneva busy. Good for the west.

answers.gripWhy: The pirate channel is tolerated on the colony's air.

situations.title: Sol Scrip
situations.question: Governor, will you let your colony print its own money?
situations.body: Charter credits run short every month. The Exchange proposes sol scrip, redeemable in ice from its stocks. Geneva's monetary office calls it secession by ledger. Arcade boards already show a scrip ticker.

answers.text: Charter the Exchange to issue ice-backed scrip
answers.sub: Exchange prints sol scrip; the treasury takes it for levies.

reasons.lme: We print the money. The arcade becomes the colony's bank.
reasons.fam: Arcadian money. One more thing Geneva no longer holds.
reasons.cas: Local money the Assembly can tax and vote on.
reasons.mca: Monetary secession, licensed by the governor herself.
reasons.hac: Our bonds are in credits. Scrip is the road to default.

answers.text: Issue shift tokens for air and calories
answers.sub: Union-run labour scrip, paid per shift worked.

reasons.riw: Air earned by the hands that mine the ice.
reasons.fam: A Mars-made currency owned by the workers.
reasons.lme: Labour tokens cut the Exchange out of its own trade.
reasons.hac: Worker money and ice: the first step to seizure.
reasons.hsd: Allocation by token undercuts the certified ration.

answers.text: Issue Directorate kilowatt credits instead
answers.sub: Scrip backed by certified power, metered by the Control Ring.

reasons.hsd: Money tied to measured margins cannot be inflated.
reasons.upa: An engineered currency. Utopia runs on the same idea.
reasons.lme: The Ring controls the money; the Exchange loses its bank.
reasons.mca: Any colonial money is monetary secession, metered or not.
reasons.riw: Engineers metering our wages in kilowatts. No.

situations.title: Under the Floor
situations.question: Governor, oxygen is under the floor. What will you tell Geneva?
situations.body: Margin report: oxygen at 141 days, 39 below the Charter floor of 180. Article 31 allows a Margin Emergency. The Directorate offers to re-baseline against expected spares. Helion-Ares bondholders read every report.

answers.text: Report the breach to the Charter Authority today
answers.sub: The 141-day figure goes to Geneva, certified and unedited.

reasons.mca: The Charter's floor is reported as the Charter requires.
reasons.aco: The chain to Geneva holds, by the book.
reasons.hsd: Our certified figure goes out unaltered.
reasons.hac: A reported breach sends our bond price down.
reasons.lme: Earth traders will price the colony as failing.

answers.text: Declare a Margin Emergency under Article 31
answers.sub: The Directorate allocates power and air; Assembly sittings suspend votes.

reasons.hsd: The gauges decide now, as they always should have.
reasons.upa: Engineers in command. A governor Utopia understands.
reasons.cas: The margins taken from the Assembly by decree.
reasons.lme: Emergency allocation means our stock gets requisitioned.
reasons.riw: Directorate rule over the halls, and no say for crews.

answers.gripWhy: Emergency powers take allocation out of elected hands.

answers.text: Re-baseline quietly to calm the bondholders
answers.sub: Spares counted early; the breach stays off the report.

reasons.hac: No breach on paper, no run on our bonds.
reasons.lme: The arcade trades another quarter without panic.
reasons.mca: A hidden breach of the Charter floor. Grounds for recall.
reasons.hsd: Counting spares not installed is cooking the margin.
reasons.riw: Our crews breathe the real figure, not the paper one.

answers.gripWhy: The true reserve is kept from Geneva and the street.

situations.title: The Charter Oath
situations.question: Governor, will you administer Geneva's oath to the Mars-born?
situations.body: The roll counts 11,400 Mars-born. Geneva's new instruction: Earth citizenship only after a Charter oath, sworn before a roll clerk. Free Arcadia has called roll-card burnings in the Erebus concourse.

answers.text: Administer the oath; no oath, no Earth passport
answers.sub: Roll clerks swear every Mars-born; refusers lose Earth citizenship.

reasons.mca: Every Mars-born bound to the Charter by oath.
reasons.aco: Sworn citizens, and a clear list of who refused.
reasons.fam: The oath is our red line. They will burn the cards.
reasons.cas: Citizenship by loyalty test, imposed without a vote.
reasons.riw: Our young crews forced to swear to Geneva.

answers.gripWhy: Citizenship tied to a loyalty oath, policed by clerks.

answers.text: Refuse the oath; register Mars-born as Arcadians
answers.sub: The roll lists them as Arcadian-born, no Earth oath required.

reasons.fam: Arcadians on paper at last. No leash, no oath.
reasons.cas: The self-government bloc wins its first written recognition.
reasons.mca: A governor who refuses the Charter's own roll.
reasons.aco: We cannot police a roll Geneva no longer recognises.
reasons.upa: A separate people means a separate partner for us.

answers.gripWhy: Citizenship stops being a test of loyalty.

situations.title: Common Kitchens
situations.question: Governor, will you feed the tube from common kitchens?
situations.body: Calories are down with the storm-dimmed decks. The RIWU wants communal kitchens in every tube block, staffed by its crews. Utopia Planitia offers two tonnes of algae protein a month. The Exchange food stalls stand to lose their trade.

answers.text: Open union kitchens with Utopian algae
answers.sub: RIWU crews cook; Utopian protein fills the pots.

reasons.riw: Common stock, shared by those who earn it.
reasons.upa: Utopian protein on every tube table. Influence by the bowl.
reasons.fam: The tube eats together, and not from Geneva.
reasons.lme: Free kitchens shut every food stall in the arcade.
reasons.mca: Arcadians fed by Utopia. A dependency we forbid.

answers.text: License Exchange stalls to sell subsidised meals
answers.sub: Treasury pays the stalls; private cooks feed the blocks.

reasons.lme: Paid contracts for every stall in the tube.
reasons.hac: Private supply, not union councils. Sound policy.
reasons.riw: Profit off hungry crews, on the treasury's tab.
reasons.upa: Our algae offer refused for arcade margins.
reasons.fam: Merchants selling Mars-born their own rations back.

situations.title: The Arcadian Congress
situations.question: Governor, will you give their Congress a voice in your decrees?
situations.body: Three hundred block delegates met in the basalt gallery under the two-moon banner. They call it the Arcadian Congress. They ask a reading of every decree before you sign. Geneva calls it a parallel authority.

answers.text: Recognise the Congress as a consultative body
answers.sub: Every decree goes to the gallery for reading first.

reasons.fam: The Arcadian people now have a chamber the governor heeds.
reasons.upa: A second authority in the tube. We can talk to it.
reasons.mca: Recognition of an authority beside the Charter. Our red line.
reasons.cas: A rival chamber in the tube outflanks the elected Assembly.
reasons.aco: The governor blesses a body that harbours the Pressure Cells.

answers.gripWhy: A street body gains a formal say over decrees.

answers.text: Fold its delegates into union block councils
answers.sub: Delegates sit on RIWU allocation councils, not as a Congress.

reasons.riw: Block councils grow, and allocation moves toward the crews.
reasons.cas: No rival chamber. The Assembly stays the only one.
reasons.fam: Our Congress dissolved into union committees.
reasons.hsd: Block councils meddling in allocation. Margins by show of gloves.
reasons.mca: Union councils are still councils outside the Charter.

situations.title: The Tankers Stand Idle
situations.question: Governor, will you write the union's say into law to end this?
situations.body: The tankers at Ice Field 7 have been idle for nine sols. The water reserve stands at 231 days and falls a day a sol. All 2,900 RIWU members are out. Kamau-Quispe will end the strike for one thing only: a union seat on allocation, voted into Assembly law.

answers.text: Send a Union Seat Bill to the Assembly
answers.sub: The RIWU gets a legal vote on air and water allocation.

reasons.riw: A seat in law outlasts any governor's promise.
reasons.cas: The Assembly writes the settlement and gains weight.
reasons.hsd: Union votes on margins mean politics in the gauges.
reasons.hac: A union veto over ice threatens our export quotas.
reasons.aco: Strikers rewarded means more strikes to police.

answers.gripWhy: Power over allocation is shared with an elected union.

answers.text: Run the tankers with Directorate crews
answers.sub: Certified controllers drive the tankers; strikers lose their shift rations.

reasons.riw: Directorate scabs in our tankers, and our rations cut.
reasons.hsd: Certified hands restore the water line on schedule.
reasons.hac: The ice moves again and the contracts hold.
reasons.fam: Mars-born crews are starved back to work.
reasons.cas: The Assembly is bypassed on a colony-wide crisis.

answers.gripWhy: Strikers are cut off and replaced by order.

answers.text: Invoke the Charter essential-services clause
answers.sub: The strike is declared unlawful; the Constabulary escorts tankers out.

reasons.aco: Clear Charter law puts officers behind the tankers.
reasons.mca: Charter law, not union terms, keeps the water running.
reasons.riw: Armed police at the pickets crosses our red line.
reasons.fam: Geneva's clause turned on Arcadian workers.
reasons.cas: An unlawful strike declared without the Assembly's vote.

answers.gripWhy: A strike is outlawed under emergency Charter powers.

situations.title: Brownout Order
situations.question: Which domes go dark first, Governor, and will you take Utopia's cells?
situations.body: Reactor Two scrammed at 04:12. Domes 2 to 5 face 22 sols of brownout. Oxygen sits at 141 days, below the 180-day floor. Utopia's rovers can bring fuel cells in eleven sols. Someone's lights go first.

answers.text: Shed load by the Directorate's margin table
answers.sub: Tube blocks go dark first; the plants and medical stay lit.

reasons.hsd: Our margin table, followed to the line.
reasons.aco: A fixed schedule is easier to police.
reasons.fam: The Mars-born tube is dark again, as always.
reasons.riw: Crew quarters dark while we keep the halls running.
reasons.cas: No member was asked whose district goes dark.

answers.gripWhy: The engineers decide who loses power, by fiat.

answers.text: Keep the tube lit, take Utopia's cells
answers.sub: The Mars-born districts are lit first; Utopian rovers cross the plain.

reasons.fam: The tube is lit by Martians helping Martians.
reasons.upa: Our rovers make Utopia Arcadia's true rescuer.
reasons.mca: Rescue by a rival settlement erodes the Charter guarantee.
reasons.hac: Utopian cells undercut our supply contracts.
reasons.hsd: Uncertified foreign cells on our grid.

answers.text: Let the blocks bid power credits for supply
answers.sub: Those who pay keep their lights; the Exchange runs the auction.

reasons.lme: Our brokers run the market for scarce watts.
reasons.hac: Priced power proves the market model works.
reasons.riw: Crews can't outbid merchants for their own light.
reasons.fam: Air and light sold to the highest bidder.
reasons.cas: An auction decided outside the levy chamber.

situations.title: Slots on Nine Ships
situations.question: How will you split the fleet's cargo slots, Governor?
situations.body: Window Fleet loading closes in Geneva in 30 days. Nine ships, and Helion-Ares holds the slots. The Exchange wants room for coffee, textiles and wine at paying rates. The Directorate wants every tonne for electrolysis stacks and reactor parts.

answers.text: Sell a third of slots to Exchange cargo
answers.sub: Paying luxuries ride along; the treasury takes a slot fee.

reasons.lme: Real coffee in the arcade, and margins with it.
reasons.hac: Paid slots service our cargo contracts.
reasons.hsd: Every crate of wine is a missing reactor seal.
reasons.riw: Luxuries for merchants while crews breathe dust.
reasons.cas: The slot fee eases the levy fight.

answers.text: Every tonne goes to machinery
answers.sub: Stacks, seals and reactor parts only; no luxuries at all.

reasons.hsd: Margins come before every comfort.
reasons.mca: Spares on the manifest show Geneva rescue at work.
reasons.lme: Our paying cargo is barred from the ships.
reasons.hac: Unpaid machinery slots eat our freight margins.

answers.text: Allocate slots by crew-council vote
answers.sub: RIWU councils list what the halls need most.

reasons.riw: The people who fix the halls choose the parts.
reasons.fam: Settlers decide, not Geneva or the Exchange.
reasons.hsd: Union lists replace our certified needs survey.
reasons.lme: Councils will never vote a slot for trade.
reasons.hac: Our slots allocated by a union show of gloves.

answers.gripWhy: Cargo decisions pass to elected crew councils.

situations.title: Flags Over the Dead

carrier.name: Benedikt Oduya
carrier.role: Chaplain of the Chapel of the Long Night

situations.question: Governor, under which flag will you let the Sabatier dead be mourned?
situations.body: Two operators died in the Train 3 fire. Chaplain Oduya has booked Dome Square for a memorial under the Charter flag. Free Arcadia says one of the dead was Mars-born and wants the rust-red banner. Dustline calls the Charter flag an insult to the dead.

answers.text: Hold the memorial under the Charter flag
answers.sub: The Charter Hymn plays; the Constabulary guards the square.

reasons.mca: The Charter honours its dead, all of them.
reasons.aco: A guarded square under one flag stays orderly.
reasons.fam: Geneva's flag over a Martian coffin.
reasons.riw: Our dead, and Earth's hymn drowns the work songs.
reasons.cas: The governor picked a side at a funeral.

answers.text: Fly the Arcadian banner over the dead
answers.sub: Duct-drums in Dome Square; the Charter flag stays furled.

reasons.fam: The two moons over Dome Square, at last.
reasons.riw: Settlers mourn our crewmates their own way.
reasons.cas: The governor listens to the settlers' mood.
reasons.mca: A secessionist banner raised in Dome 1 itself.
reasons.aco: Officers ordered to guard a Free Arcadia rally.

answers.gripWhy: A banned banner flies with your blessing.

situations.title: The Veto at First Reading
situations.question: Will you use the Charter veto on the Self-Government Bill now?
situations.body: Speaker Ferreira-Oyelaran has tabled the Self-Government Bill. The whips count 31 of 50 seats for it; 26 carry. A veto now kills it before debate. Geneva is watching the link.

answers.text: Let first reading proceed, no veto
answers.sub: The bill is debated openly; you stay neutral on paper.

reasons.cas: The chamber does real business at last.
reasons.fam: Self-government on the floor, not in the tube.
reasons.lme: Local rule could mean local trade terms.
reasons.mca: A governor who lets secession be read aloud.
reasons.aco: Officers swore to a Charter you let be debated away.

answers.gripWhy: The Assembly is free to debate secession.

answers.text: Veto it under the Charter
answers.sub: The bill dies; the Assembly loses its main business.

reasons.mca: The Charter's veto used as Geneva intended.
reasons.aco: The chain of command up to Geneva stands.
reasons.cas: Thirty-one votes erased by one Earth clause.
reasons.fam: Proof that the Charter is a leash.

answers.gripWhy: An elected majority is silenced by veto.

answers.text: Amend it into a trade-autonomy bill
answers.sub: Levy and tariff powers for the Assembly; no secession clause.

reasons.lme: Tariff powers in local hands help our trade.
reasons.hac: Trade autonomy without repudiation suits our bonds.
reasons.cas: Real levy powers, if not the whole bill.
reasons.fam: They sold our homeland for tariff tables.
reasons.mca: Any Assembly power grab is a precedent.

situations.title: Quarters for the Marines
situations.question: Where will you quarter the 400 Marines, Governor, and under whose command?
situations.body: Geneva confirms 400 Charter Marines aboard the Window Fleet. The Assembly demands they stay at the Pad Field, outside the domes. Commandant Osei-Brandt wants them under his command inside Dome 1.

answers.text: Place the Marines under Osei-Brandt in Dome 1
answers.sub: One chain of command, from the Constabulary up to Geneva.

reasons.aco: The Marines reinforce us instead of replacing us.
reasons.mca: The garrison serves the Charter's lawful police.
reasons.cas: Our demand for the Pad Field was ignored.
reasons.fam: Earth soldiers inside the domes: an occupation.
reasons.upa: A Marine force in the colony's heart, armed westward.

answers.gripWhy: An armed garrison is placed inside the domes.

answers.text: Pad Field only, barred from the tube
answers.sub: The Marines stay outside; the tube locks stay in settler hands.

reasons.cas: Our vote decided where they sleep.
reasons.fam: Not one Earth boot below the basalt line.
reasons.upa: Marines kept at the pads point nowhere.
reasons.aco: We are left outgunned and passed over.
reasons.mca: Our battalion is fenced off like a threat.

answers.text: Assign them to guard the plants
answers.sub: Marines post at reactors and electrolysis under Directorate orders.

reasons.hsd: The plants are guarded from strikes and sabotage.
reasons.mca: The Marines serve, whoever directs them.
reasons.riw: Armed troops in the halls: our red line.
reasons.aco: Directorate orders, not ours, run the Marines.
reasons.upa: Marines garrison the ice we want to lease.

situations.title: Ten Hours for the Hull
situations.question: Will you make every adult serve ten hours a week on maintenance?
situations.body: Seals are failing faster than crews can fix them. The Directorate's Systems Service would take every adult from 16 to 60 for ten hours a week. The RIWU calls it scab conscription. Free Arcadia says Mars-born kids will scrub Earth's ducts.

answers.text: Decree the Systems Service
answers.sub: Ten hours a week, logged on certification cards.

reasons.hsd: Ten thousand hands on the seal backlog.
reasons.aco: Logged service cards make a tidy register.
reasons.hac: Unpaid maintenance protects our modules.
reasons.riw: Conscripts doing union work for nothing.
reasons.fam: Martian youth drafted to patch Earth's hulls.
reasons.lme: Ten hours lost from every shop and stall.

answers.gripWhy: Compulsory labour is imposed by decree.

answers.text: Hire maintenance through RIWU crews instead
answers.sub: Union rates and union rosters, paid from the treasury.

reasons.riw: Paid union work, not a labour draft.
reasons.fam: No Mars-born teenager in a duct.
reasons.hsd: Union rosters, not our schedules, set repair order.
reasons.hac: Union rates for work on our modules.

situations.title: The Council Takes the Plant
situations.question: Will you let the union take Helion-Ares's ice plant, Governor?
situations.body: Plant workers at Ice Field 7 have elected a council and voted to run the processing plant in common. Helion-Ares built it and holds the deed. Sørlie-Tan threatens suit in Earth courts and a freeze on spares.

answers.text: Vest the plant in the workers' council
answers.sub: Common ownership; the RIWU council runs the ice line.

reasons.riw: The ice belongs to those who dig it.
reasons.fam: Earth capital loses its grip on Arcadian ice.
reasons.hac: Confiscation of our plant: our red line.
reasons.lme: Today their plant, tomorrow our decks.
reasons.mca: Seizing Earth property invites Earth courts.

answers.text: Broker a share sale to Exchange investors
answers.sub: Helion-Ares sells 40 percent locally; workers get bonuses.

reasons.lme: A stake in the colony's ice at last.
reasons.hac: We sell a share on our terms and keep control.
reasons.cas: Local owners keep ice money in Arcadia.
reasons.riw: Bonuses instead of ownership: a bribe.

answers.text: Take the plant into colony ownership
answers.sub: Arcadia's ice is held by the settlement, not by Earth.

reasons.fam: Air Is Ours, and now the ice too.
reasons.cas: The Assembly gains a plant to govern.
reasons.riw: Better the colony than the Consortium.
reasons.hac: Expropriation by a colony that owes us.
reasons.mca: A settlement seizing assets acts like a state.

situations.title: Default Day
situations.question: The bond has lapsed. Will you grant field rights, default, or seek Geneva?
situations.body: The six-month rollover has expired. ₵1.2 billion of principal is due, and the treasury cannot pay it. Helion-Ares threatens default proceedings and a freeze on the fleet's cargo unless it gets 30-year field rights. The Assembly is debating repudiation.

answers.text: Grant 30-year field rights for a rollover
answers.sub: Default is averted; the ice fields are Helion-Ares's until 2122.

reasons.hac: Thirty years of fields secures our bonds.
reasons.lme: Credit keeps flowing to the arcade.
reasons.riw: Our ice is sold for a generation.
reasons.fam: Arcadia's ice is mortgaged to Earth until 2122.
reasons.cas: The levy chamber was bypassed on the debt.

answers.text: Back repudiation of the colonial debt
answers.sub: Arcadia refuses the Consortium's bonds as Earth's debt, not its own.

reasons.fam: We never signed Earth's debts.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's motion carries the day.
reasons.riw: No more shifts worked to pay bondholders.
reasons.hac: Repudiation: everything we feared from Areanists.
reasons.mca: Repudiating the debt comes one step before secession.
reasons.lme: Our Earth credit lines die with the bonds.

answers.text: Ask Geneva to guarantee the debt
answers.sub: The Charter Authority stands surety and oversees the treasury.

reasons.mca: An Earth guarantee binds Arcadia to the Charter.
reasons.aco: Geneva's backing steadies the colony's paymaster.
reasons.hac: A Concord guarantee is better than a default.
reasons.cas: Earth auditors will now run our levy.
reasons.fam: Geneva buys the colony's leash with its debt.

situations.title: The Cut Relay
situations.question: The relay mast is down. Will you talk, hunt or rebuild?
situations.body: The Pressure Cells cut the Charter relay mast on Ridge 2 overnight. Geneva traffic now runs on one backup dish. Juno Arrieta claims it on Dustline. From detention, Ezra Valdivia sends word: he will disown the Cells in public if you open talks with him.

answers.text: Open talks with Valdivia in detention
answers.sub: He disowns the Cells; you treat with Free Arcadia.

reasons.fam: Our founder at the table splits the Cells from the movement.
reasons.cas: Talks bring the self-government bloc into the room.
reasons.riw: Talking beats sweeps through our members' blocks.
reasons.aco: You reward the men who cut a Charter mast.
reasons.mca: Negotiating with a sedition suspect is a precedent for secession.

answers.gripWhy: The governor treats with the movement instead of policing it.

answers.text: Order a Constabulary hunt for the Pressure Cells
answers.sub: Article 19 sweeps through the tube blocks.

reasons.aco: At last a clear order to take the tube back.
reasons.mca: Charter property was attacked; Charter law answers.
reasons.fam: Every Mars-born youth becomes a suspect in his own block.
reasons.cas: Sweeps without warrants insult the Assembly's members.
reasons.riw: Our crews live in those blocks and get searched too.

answers.gripWhy: Mass searches under the sedition article.

answers.text: Rebuild the mast under Directorate guard; no talks
answers.sub: Hardened relay, engineers' cordon, no deal with anyone.

reasons.hsd: Comms are a system; we fix systems, not grievances.
reasons.upa: A governor leaning on engineers suits Utopia.
reasons.fam: Ignored again; the Cells will say only cutting works.
reasons.aco: Directorate cordons do our job without our command.
reasons.mca: Geneva wanted the culprits caught, not a better mast.

situations.title: The Ten-Year Plan
situations.question: One budget, two futures. Where will you sink your credits?
situations.body: The Directorate's ten-year plan is on your desk. Option one: deep drilling in the expanded crater with leased Utopian rigs. Option two: expanding the Erebus lava tube under basalt cover. The treasury can fund one. Dome 3 still leaks 0.4 percent a sol.

answers.text: Drill the crater with Utopian rigs
answers.sub: Deep ice for the margins; Utopia's machines in our fields.

reasons.hsd: Deep ice is the only margin that lasts ten years.
reasons.upa: Our rigs in Arcadia mean leases and influence.
reasons.riw: Drilling means shifts and new crews.
reasons.hac: Utopian rigs eat into our export claims.
reasons.mca: Geneva will not have Utopia drilling a Charter colony.

answers.text: Sink the budget into the lava tube
answers.sub: New basalt terraces for living under rock.

reasons.fam: The tube is Arcadian ground; build our homeland there.
reasons.cas: Members' districts get the housing they asked for.
reasons.lme: Terraces need shops and fabrication contracts.
reasons.hsd: Housing before ice is a margin built on sand.
reasons.upa: No rigs, no lease, no foothold.

situations.title: A Seat at Review
situations.question: Geneva offers a Commission seat for your public word. Will you give it?
situations.body: The Charter Review Commission opens its hearings in June. Commissioner Mwangi-Rousseau offers your nominee a seat on it. The price: you back renewal publicly before the Assembly votes. The self-government bloc holds 31 of 50 seats.

answers.text: Back renewal publicly and take the seat
answers.sub: Your nominee sits in Geneva; you stand with the Charter.

reasons.mca: A governor who campaigns for renewal is what we appointed.
reasons.aco: A clear Charter line keeps our chain of command.
reasons.hac: Renewal keeps our bonds under Earth courts.
reasons.fam: The governor picks Geneva over the Mars-born.
reasons.cas: You prejudge the Assembly's vote before it sits.

answers.gripWhy: The governor takes Geneva's side against the chamber.

answers.text: Refuse; the settlers decide renewal
answers.sub: No seat, no endorsement, the vote stays local.

reasons.fam: Arcadia's future is not Geneva's to buy.
reasons.cas: The Assembly's vote stays the Assembly's.
reasons.upa: Geneva's grip loosens; Utopia gains room.
reasons.mca: A governor neutral on the Charter is a governor in doubt.
reasons.aco: Officers want to know whose writ they enforce.

answers.text: Trade your backing for dominion terms and bonds
answers.sub: Endorse a revised Charter with trade rights and debt secured.

reasons.lme: Dominion trade terms open the Exchange to Earth markets.
reasons.hac: Bonds written into the Charter are bonds repaid.
reasons.cas: A revised Charter gives the levy power we want.
reasons.mca: Geneva does not haggle over its Charter.
reasons.fam: Dominion is still a leash, just a gilded one.

situations.title: The Extradition Order
situations.question: Geneva wants Valdivia on the return leg. Will you hand him over?
situations.body: The bench acquitted Ezra Valdivia of sedition and gave him 90 sols for unlawful assembly. Now the Charter Authority orders him extradited to Earth on the fleet's return leg. Duct-drums already pound in the Erebus concourse. Mira Solheim reads the order aloud on Dustline every hour.

answers.text: Execute the extradition order on the return leg
answers.sub: He serves his sols, then ships Earthward under guard.

reasons.mca: Charter law reaches every settler, Mars-born or not.
reasons.aco: Shipping him off ends the rallies at the source.
reasons.fam: Extradition is our red line; this is war on us.
reasons.cas: Overriding the bench's verdict mocks the trial.
reasons.riw: Our tube members will walk off over this.

answers.gripWhy: Deporting a popular leader against the bench's sentence.

answers.text: Refuse; he serves his 90 sols here
answers.sub: Arcadian sentence, Arcadian cell, then release.

reasons.fam: Arcadians are judged and held in Arcadia.
reasons.cas: The mixed bench's sentence stands as the last word.
reasons.upa: Defying Geneva shows Arcadia can stand alone.
reasons.mca: Refusing a Charter order is a step toward secession.
reasons.aco: He walks out in 90 sols and rallies again.

answers.gripWhy: The governor shields a dissident from Geneva.

answers.text: Release him to RIWU custody pending appeal
answers.sub: Union bond, union hall, union guarantee he stays.

reasons.riw: Our guarantee proves the union keeps order better.
reasons.fam: Free under the workers' roof beats Earth's cells.
reasons.hsd: A union holding prisoners near the plants is risk.
reasons.aco: Custody belongs to officers, not a picket hall.
reasons.mca: Bail to a union is no answer to a Charter order.

answers.gripWhy: A convicted man is freed into union hands.

situations.title: Water by Block

carrier.name: Amaru Kipkemboi
carrier.role: RIWU block steward, Tube Sector C

situations.question: The blocks share their own water now. Will you make it law?
situations.body: Tube residents have elected block committees in 34 blocks. They share out the water ration by raised glove. The RIWU asks you to give their tallies legal force over the Directorate's meters. Directorate controllers say the committees already read 6 percent over the plan.

answers.text: Give the block committees legal force over meters
answers.sub: Elected committees allocate; Directorate meters only measure.

reasons.riw: The people who haul the ice now share the water.
reasons.fam: Tube blocks governing themselves is self-government in practice.
reasons.cas: Elected bodies with real powers strengthen our case.
reasons.hsd: Allocation by show of hands will drain the reserve.
reasons.lme: Committees will ration our members' private allowances next.

answers.gripWhy: Allocation passes from the plant to elected committees.

answers.text: Keep the meters under Directorate control
answers.sub: Committees may advise; the certified figure decides.

reasons.hsd: Water is a margin, not a vote.
reasons.aco: One authority over the valves means fewer fights.
reasons.hac: Engineers on the meters protect plant output.
reasons.riw: You refuse the workers their own common stock.
reasons.fam: Dome 1 keeps its hand on the tube's taps.

answers.gripWhy: The governor overrules elected committees.

situations.title: Berths and Names
situations.question: Earth buyers want berths and names. Will you sell Arcadia's landmarks?
